<reflection>
The second experiment (high substrate concentration) yielded fitting results where M7 remains slightly better than M6, M8, and M17, but all four are within a narrow NLL range (-40.15 to -39.68). This indicates that the high-substrate condition did not strongly discriminate among the top candidates. My aim for the second turn was to stress the system to reveal differences in saturation, deactivation, or activation; while some separation occurred (M7 slightly best), the differences remain small. Therefore, more discriminative conditions are needed.
</reflection>
<hypothesis>
The leading candidates (M7, M6, M8, M17) differ in how product affects the reaction. M17 features irreversible product-induced deactivation (P + catS → inactive), which should cause strong inhibition when product is present initially. In contrast, M7 (ternary complex) and M6/M8 (catalyst activation) involve only reversible product inhibition (if any). To test this, I propose an experiment with added initial product (0.5 M) while keeping substrate (2.0 M) and catalyst (0.02 M) constant relative to the first experiment. This will directly probe whether product irreversibly deactivates the catalyst (M17) or simply slows the reaction reversibly (others).

**Contrastive predictions:**
- **M17**: Initial product immediately deactivates a portion of the catalyst-substrate complex, leading to a significantly reduced initial rate and an early plateau in product formation. The final conversion will be lower compared to the first experiment (no product).
- **M7**: Product may reversibly inhibit the reaction by shifting the equilibrium of the second step (catS2 ⇌ P + catS). The initial rate will be moderately reduced, but the reaction will proceed steadily without an early plateau, resembling reversible inhibition.
- **M6/M8**: Product reversibly inhibits the catalytic steps (S + cat* ⇌ cat*S and cat*S ⇌ P + cat*). The initial rate will be lower, but no irreversible loss of active catalyst occurs, so the progress curve will show slower but persistent conversion.

The key observable is whether the reaction stalls early (M17) or continues progressing (others), and the magnitude of initial rate suppression relative to the first experiment.
</hypothesis>
